text:
lina: quick heads-up — after enabling remat for the 40B workload on the 16TP/8PP cluster we see ~12% P99 increase and periodic throughput dips. traces show pronounced all-reduce spikes at certain remat boundary layers.

sam: can you paste the trace and the perf summary?

lina: pasted minimal trace snippet below (from perf-trace):
```
[trace] layer_23 remat_start -> compute -> remat_end | allreduce start @0.234s -> finish @0.278s
[trace] layer_47 remat_start -> compute -> remat_end | allreduce start @0.492s -> finish @0.558s
aggregate: allreduce bursts align with last op of recompute region, latency amplification x1.9 vs baseline
```

maria: hmm — sounds like compute/comm overlap is collapsing when remat forces synchronous recompute at boundary layers. are we folding micro-batches so all PP ranks hit reduce simultaneously?

lina: yes, current micro-batch aligner groups 8 microbatches per pipeline stage, so all PP ranks reach the boundary in lockstep.

arjun: network metrics? are we seeing NIC saturations or IPC stalls?

lina: NIC not saturated, but per-host socket queues spike. host-level p99 queue latency goes from 0.9ms -> 3.2ms at those windows.

jess: another angle — KV cache prefetch traffic can coincide with recompute. our prefetch for long-contexts triggers synchronous kv sync near layer boundaries. any kv logs?

lina: good call — found overlapping kv sync @ layer_47 in trace. ordering: recompute -> kv_sync -> allreduce. that serializes everything.

sam: couple quick ideas to try: stagger recompute boundaries across PP stages, or change kernel selection to allow earlier reduce-scatter overlap. also try moving KV sync to async prefetch with lower priority.

maria: i prototyped a "staggered_boundaries" scheduler in local tests — it shifts remat cut points by stage index mod N to avoid simultaneous allreduce. config snippet:
```yaml
recompute_scheduler: staggered_boundaries
stagger_stride: 1  # shift boundary by 1 layer per stage
apply_to: [transformer_block_remat_points]
```

lina: ran a short canary with staggered_boundaries + async-kv-prefetch: results below
```
baseline P99 = 210ms
remat (no changes) P99 = 235ms (+12%)
remat + staggered_boundaries P99 = 218ms (+3.8%)
remat + staggered_boundaries + async-kv P99 = 212ms (+1%)
throughput steady state improved by ~4% over remat baseline
```

arjun: promising. do we pay extra memory / activation slot overhead for shifting boundaries?

maria: negligible — we only adjust which layers are recomputed per stage; total recompute work unchanged, just redistributed. small code change in scheduler.

sam: did you run kernel-selection profiling? maybe remat made us pick a slower matmul kernel for the recompute path due to different sequence lengths.

lina: grabbed kernel histogram for matmul on remat path:
```
selected_kernels: [cuda_gemm_v1: 60%, cuda_gemm_v2: 35%, fallback_mma: 5%]
post-stagger selected_kernels: [cuda_gemm_v1: 65%, cuda_gemm_v2: 30%, fallback_mma: 5%]
```
change small but helped overlap.

jess: for KV: async prefetch implemented with a low-priority background thread and a token-bucket limiter so it yields during high comm. no correctness issues in canary.

arjun: good. next step — add a perf job that compares: (A) remat baseline, (B) remat + staggered_boundaries, (C) remat + staggered_boundaries + async-kv, and capture detailed per-layer allreduce timing + NIC queue histograms. can we schedule a run on prod-sized infra? @dev-bot please kick off perf-suite-pp-tp-40b with those three configs.

dev-bot: scheduled perf-suite-pp-tp-40b (#4729) on 2026-03-18T10:12Z. run ids: A=4729-a, B=4729-b, C=4729-c. will post aggregated metrics to this thread when done. :robot_face:

sam: one more experiment to consider — opportunistic kernel offload: detect remat boundary allreduce windows and prefer reduce-scatter primitives that overlap earlier (we have a backend flag `prefer_overlap_reduce_scatter`). toggling that could reduce spike width.

maria: yes, i can add an optimizer pass that toggles the flag when recompute density > threshold. snippet:
```python
if recompute_density(stage) > 0.25:
    set_kernel_hint(stage, 'prefer_overlap_reduce_scatter', True)
```

lina: for traceability, i added a trace tag `remat_stagger=v1` to the canary runs. once perf-batch completes we'll compare flame graphs and per-op timing.

arjun: if perf-suite validates, we should roll into a controlled canary on Dedicated next week. also update the Optimize heuristics so customers with remat enabled get a suggested "staggered_boundaries" toggle.

jess: i'll draft a short doc for the KV prefetch feature and the tradeoffs (latency vs early warm/cache hit).

sam: great. if dev-bot posts results, i'll pull out a PR with the scheduler + kernel-hint pass.

lina: thanks all — will paste perf-suite outputs when available. for now action items: maria add kernel-hint optimizer, jess docs + async-kv PR, sam PR for scheduler + tests, dev-bot run and report.

(ended)
